concept.title: Data Flow in a Home Network
concept.shortdesc: Data flow describes how information moves between user devices, the home network, and Internet resources. Understanding data flow helps users understand how network components work together to provide connectivity.

section.title: Overview
section.p: When a client device communicates with another device or an Internet resource, data travels through one or more network components.
In a typical home network, the directs data between connected devices and the Internet.

section.title: Data Flow to the Internet
section.p: When a client device accesses a website, online application, or cloud service, data passes through the home network before reaching its destination.

fig.title: Data flow between a client device and the Internet

section.p: The response follows the same path back to the client device.

section.title: Data Flow Within the Home Network
section.p: Devices on the same network can exchange data without using an Internet connection.
For example, a laptop can send a document to a printer or access files stored on a network storage device.

fig.title: Data flow within the home network

section.title: Role of Network Components
section.p: Each network component performs a specific role in the flow of data.

ul.li: The ISP provides the Internet connection.
Client devices send and receive data.

section.title: Advanced Information
section.p: Data is transmitted as packets across the network.
The examines packet information and forwards traffic to the appropriate destination.
Network devices use addressing information and routing decisions to ensure that packets reach their intended destination.
